html:
The Tillamook are a Coast Salish people of the northern Oregon coast, the southernmost speakers of a Salish language. Their villages stood on Tillamook Bay and the Nehalem, Nestucca and Siletz rivers.

They fished salmon, gathered shellfish and hunted sea mammals, and traded with the Clatsop and other Chinook to the north. In 1806 William Clark of the Lewis and Clark Expedition crossed to their coast to buy blubber from a stranded whale. Disease cut their numbers sharply in the early 1800s. Their land was taken without a ratified treaty, and the survivors went to the Siletz and Grand Ronde reservations. The last fluent speaker of Tillamook died in 1970. The Salmon River people were one of their southern bands.
